title: Globally-consistent usage ledger with tenant restriction hooks
creator: Marco Nguyen
description:
Problem: Console usage analytics stream currently fans out writes and materialized views without a first-class enforcement layer for tenant-level residency constraints. That leads to accidental cross-region replication for some tenants during failover and causes compliance risk for enterprise customers in regulated regions.

Goal: Implement a globally-consistent usage ledger abstraction and a lightweight tenant restriction hook layer that ensures writes and eventual analytic projections respect tenant residency policies while preserving low-latency reads and permitted cross-region fallbacks.

Scope: backend services that ingest token-level events, the replication orchestration layer, and the materialized view builders used by the Console. UI work for policy editing is out of scope for this ticket (handled by PM-4312).
acceptance_criteria: All tenant write events are annotated with authoritative residency metadata at ingest time
Replication router rejects or quarantines any attempt to mirror tenant data into non-permitted regions and raises alert with tenant+event details
Materialized views for per-tenant dashboards only include records from permitted regions unless an explicit cross-region fallback flag is set
Measured cross-region replication rate for restricted-tenants is <= 0.1% during normal operations and explained in runbook when exceeded
End-to-end tests that simulate region evacuation and automatic fallback complete without violating residency policy
Logs/audit trail include tenant id, origin region, applied residency policy version, and routing decision for every write (retention policy set by retention-service)
Performance: median ingest latency impact < 6ms p50 and no change to 99th percentile beyond 12ms for production traffic profile
design_decisions: Add a small authoritative 'tenant_residency' field to the canonical usage event envelope at the first write gateway (edge-proxy) to avoid repeated policy lookups downstream
Introduce a replication-policy evaluation component in the replication router instead of piggybacking on the mirror service to centralize decisioning
Quarantine flow: rejected cross-region writes go to a tenant-quarantine topic with immutable append-only ledger entries to preserve for audit and eventual operator-driven replay
Make residency rules versioned and pin the policy version in the event envelope so downstream rebuilds are deterministic

Materialized view builders must accept an allowlist of regions; builders running in a region will filter events on permissible origin regions unless a 'policy-override' header is present from an authorized operator service
To minimize latency, TTL-based caching of tenant residency lookups will be used at the gateway with soft invalidation hooks from the tenant-config service
Fail-open vs fail-closed tradeoff: default is fail-closed for tenants with any residency constraints; system supports explicit emergency operator overrides documented in runbook
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag all new evaluation logic behind 'residency-ledger-enabled' controlled per-cluster
2) Deploy ingestion gateway change to a canary region with synthetic tenants; monitor latency and correctness for 48 hours
3) Enable replication-router policy evaluation in read-only mode (dry-run) for selected real tenants and surface decisions to Console dev dashboard
4) Flip quarantine path for a pilot tenant group (internal + 5 customers) with ops on-call present
5) Full rollout across Dedicated clusters after 2-week stability window and sign-off from security/compliance
6) Post-rollout: sweep to backfill quarantine topics into materialized views if operators approve replay
qa_plan: Unit tests for policy-eval with boundary residency rules
Integration tests: multi-region topology simulator that injects origin-region header and verifies router decisions
Chaos test: simulate region evacuation and ensure no restricted tenant data appears in target region logs
Regression tests for latency budgets under the svc-load profile (replay of 1 hour of prod-like traffic)
Manual verification checklist for pilot tenants (PR/ops runbook)
notes: Related legal requirement: EU customer dataset must not be replicated outside eu-central and eu-west without signed DPA extension (legal ticket LEG-1286)
We decided against embedding full policy JSON in every event to save payload size; policy version + small residency code chosen instead
Cache invalidation: tenant-config service will publish lightweight 'residency-change' events on bus for soft invalidation
We considered protocol-level encryption to lock quarantine topic but deferred to release 2025.06 due to key rotation work
